1.note: The pseudo-Metasthenes (Megasthenes) De iudicio temporum, a forgery published with pseudo-Berosus by Annius of Viterbo (Giovanni Nanni), Antiquitates, 1498. The letters (a)-(e) in the text are reference marks to de' Rossi's own comments.

2.he: ואת היותר מכל סופר שהיה נחרים כדבר לא אמון בו
2.note: Syntax obscure; rendered after the sense of the Latin (reject other writers as untrustworthy).

3.note: Hebrew transliterates Annius' king names; Latin forms in this list follow the usual Annian/Eusebian list where recognizable, but individual equivalences (e.g. Zameis, Machaleus, Belopares) are not certain.

4.note: Hebrew forms (Tiba Tiaus, Tinyaus) are corrupt; probably Sosares/Lampares and Panyas/Thinaeus of the Assyrian list. Identification uncertain.

5.he: הרג גם השליך את עצמו באש
5.note: Object of 'killed' unstated; perhaps 'killed himself and cast himself into the fire'.

6.note: Unidentified people; transliterated. Possibly a corruption connected with the name Tomyris.
